Control of the delivery of bile salts to the duodenum.
For the gallbladder to empty, it must contract with enough 
force to expel the bile and move it along the common bile duct,
and the sphincter of Oddi must relax and allow bile to ﬂ ow 
into the duodenum. Following the eating of a meal, the enzyme 
cholecystokinin (CCK) is released from the mucosa of the small 
intestine, stimulated by the hydrolytic products of digestion.
CCK stimulates the gallbladder to contract and deliver bile 
into the proximal small intestine. Bile salts are essential for 
the emulsiﬁ cation of fat that must occur before lipids can be 
digested and absorbed.
